name: GA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans D+27, among the most Democratic House seats
Incumbent Hank Johnson holds a large fundraising edge; challenger James Duffie reports none
Prediction markets price Johnson near 98 percent
No polls or expert ratings, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's D+27 lean, Johnson's incumbency and fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 98 percent leave no evidence of a competitive race, while the Republican challenger has reported no fundraising.
model.watch: Any sign of a funded challenger campaign or unexpected polling could narrow the picture, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's fourth district is one of the most Democratic-leaning House seats in the country, and Hank Johnson has held it since 2007. He is running again with a clear financial edge, having raised about $400,000 with roughly $118,000 on hand, while Republican James Duffie shows no reported fundraising. No public polls track the race and no major expert raters have weighed in, so fundamentals and market pricing carry the forecast.

Prediction markets put Johnson's chances near 98 percent, in line with the district's D+27 lean and the absence of any visible challenger operation. The lack of polling widens the uncertainty band somewhat, but nothing in the evidence points to a competitive race. Johnson is favored to win another term by a wide margin.
